newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BROKERS' 1996 MARKET SHARES - SMEHA.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BROKERS' 1996 MARKET SHARES - SMEHA.

text.p: It wasn't exactly one of its better years. The Athens bourse returned a negative 1.0 percent in dollar terms in 1996 but despite a turbulent year trading volume rose 41.1 percent to 3.97 trillion drachmas.

Hit by a messy share registration law, a surprise government backtrack on a much-touted Athens casino project and the Delta Securities scandal, the Athens bourse ranked 22nd out of 30 emerging markets in the IFC global index.
The Athens stock exchange member broker association (SMEHA) released market share rankings for 1996.

National Securities, a subsidiary of state National Bank led in market share with 16.9 percent of trading volume last year but its sizeable chunk of the business was boosted by numerous put-through trades, done for accounting purposes.
Market sources estimate these put-throughs at around 500 billion drachmas out of National's 674 billion in trading volume last year. This distorted market share rankings.
They said a more objective view of market activity as measured by average daily trading volume excluding large put-through trades would provide a more accurate picture.
Put-through trades accounted for about 10 percent of last year's trading volume. Thus, excluding National's put-through trades would lower its market share to around 5.0 percent.
Sigma Securities which led in 1995 with 9.78 percent of the business ranked second with 9.18 percent or 365 billion drachmas in 1996.
It was followed by Alpha Brokerage, a subsidiary of Alpha Credit Bank, which ended the year with 6.6 percent.
December proved to be last year's best month as volume reached 577 billion. May was the worst at 209 billion.
SMEHA provided the following data and market share rankings for 1996. The top 15 brokers shared 65.07 percent of the bourse's trading volume leaving 34.9 percent for the other 49 brokers.
